newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up on selective buying.

text.p: * Market still hounded by uncertainty over U.S. rates
Manila shares recovered some of its previous day's losses on Thursday, helped by the gains of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) and San Miguel Corp (SMC), traders said.
The main index advanced 8.37 points to 3,194.56 after Wednesday's 15.61-point fall.
Joel Mendoza, research head of Urbancorp Securities, said "the market is just moving sideways."
"Nobody wants to move aggressively. The uncertainty over U.S. interest rates will still continue," he said. The U.S. Federal Reserve Board is scheduled to meet on September 24.

Analysts said investors were buying SMC due to the news that the Lower House would back an excise tax scheme on beer which would benefit the beer and food conglomerate. SMC A shares rose 50 centavos to 40.50 pesos.
Mendoza predicted the market would trade in narrow band on Friday.
